chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: The Cigale repertoire: hard jazz, bop arrangements, beguines
summary: Butler played hard jazz with some bop and New Orleans mixed with beguines and boleros, having bop tunes sent over, and Crouch asks about Parker tunes.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What kind of music were you playing?
Oh, I'm playing hard jazz then. I was playing halfway be-bop, but then, I feel like New Orleans, they call it New Orleans. Well, mixing it up. I'd play beguines, I'd play boleros.
Oh, so you'd play a real broad repertoire.
What kind of be-bop tunes did you play? Did you play originals that you wrote or --
A fellow sent them over to me.
Did you ever play that one (humming). Fats Navarro's tunes?
I don't think that was even printed at that time, see. Because (inaudible), the music they were making over there was beautiful.
Did you ever play those counterpontal (PHONETIC) things Bird wrote like "Ma-leu-cha" Child," or "Chasin' the Bird"?
(Unintelligible), because that was worked kind of in.
